page: Amazon Web Services r8g.large is a memory-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors built on the arm64 Neoverse-V2 microarchitecture. Provisioned through the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at a clock frequency of 2.8 GHz, accompanied by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, delivering an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The instance includes 1 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates without local NVMe instance storage, and does not include hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate reliable single-core capability paired with throughput constrained by the low core count. The Neoverse-V2 core registers mid-tier performance in single-core metrics, achieving 1813.0 on Geekbench and 1707.08 on stress-ng, alongside strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 14.37 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth achieves an average 56.58 GB/sec with a PassMark memory score of 2542.74. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput falls in the lower tiers across stress-ng (3400.18) and Geekbench multi-core (3243.0), while Redis SET throughput reaches 4.47 million operations per second and web serving registers 4.9 GB/sec.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM configuration offers high memory density for workloads with moderate computational demands, reducing infrastructure overhead where licensing or instance sizing depends on core counts. The primary tradeoff is the absence of local disk drives, necessitating network-attached storage for stateful services. AWS r8g.large is suited for in-memory caching systems, lightweight relational databases, small-footprint search indexes, and backend services that require higher RAM buffers relative to thread concurrency.
description: Amazon Web Services r8g.large is a memory-optimized instance based on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V2 architecture running on the AWS Nitro system. The configuration features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs at 2.8 GHz, 16.0 GB of system memory at 8.0 GB per vCPU, 36 MB L3 cache, and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no local NVMe storage and no GPU acceleration. Benchmark measurements show consistent single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1813.0 and single-thread bzip3 decompression reaching 14.37 GB/sec, while multi-core metrics remain constrained by the two-core layout. PassMark database tests show average processing capacity at 3030.65 points, and Redis SET throughput measures 4.47 million operations per second. The instance delivers high memory density relative to core count, making it suitable for memory-intensive caching tiers, lightweight key-value stores, and small database workloads.
